fam_f0002: The annual DDB rate is exactly 2 divided by the useful life in years, computed at 50-digit precision with no rounding, so 2/11 stays unrounded.
Each year's depreciation charge is the beginning book value multiplied by the unrounded rate, and the running book value is carried forward unrounded at every step.
Exactly the elapsed-year count of depreciation steps is applied, covering years 1 through that count inclusive; zero elapsed years returns the original cost.
The charge is capped: if beginning book value times the rate exceeds beginning book value minus salvage value, the charge is set to that difference, so book value never falls below salvage value.
No switch to straight-line depreciation is made in any year; the DDB rate is applied to the declining balance every year.

The code performs no rounding at all; the returned book value is the full-precision unrounded value, and the final answer is rounded to the nearest cent with halves rounded up, applied once outside the code.
